record.paper_title: On Open Problems of Nonnegative Inverse Eigenvalues Problem
record.original_question: Given an n x n entrywise nonnegative matrix A, must there exist an n x n invertible real matrix P such that the similar matrix B = P^{-1} A P is symmetric?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $A$ be an $n \times n$ matrix with real entries satisfying $A_{ij} \ge 0$ for all $i,j$ (an entrywise nonnegative matrix). Decide whether the following statement is true: for every such $A$, there exists an invertible real matrix $P \in GL_n(\mathbb{R})$ such that $B = P^{-1} A P$ is a real symmetric matrix (i.e., $B^T = B$). If the statement is false in general, exhibit a counterexample.
artifact.status_search_result: The statement is false in general. A real matrix is similar to a real symmetric matrix only if it is diagonalizable over the reals with real eigenvalues. Nonnegative matrices can have non-real (complex conjugate) eigenvalues — for instance, the $3\times 3$ cyclic permutation matrix with rows $(0,1,0),(0,0,1),(1,0,0)$ has eigenvalues $1, e^{2\pi i/3}, e^{-2\pi i/3}$ and therefore cannot be similar to any real symmetric matrix. Thus the answer to the posed question is negative, and this is classical linear algebra rather than an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Real symmetric matrices have real eigenvalues (standard linear algebra)
status_evidence.snippet: Every real symmetric matrix is diagonalizable by an orthogonal matrix and has only real eigenvalues.
status_evidence.claim: Any matrix similar to a real symmetric matrix must have only real eigenvalues, ruling out nonnegative matrices with complex eigenvalues.
